# opnsense_nginx_http_server (Data Source)

nginx HTTP servers (**Services ▸ Nginx ▸ Configuration ▸ HTTP(S) ▸ HTTP Server**, plugin `os-nginx`).



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `id` (String) UUID of the nginx HTTP server.

### Read-Only

- `access_log_format` (String) Access Log Format. One of `main`, `main_ext`, `anonymized`, `disabled`.
- `advanced_acl_server` (String) Choose a backend for advanced authentication. If you don't have one, configure it under System -> Access -> Servers. If nothing is configured, the local database is used.
- `block_nonpublic_data` (Boolean) Blocks files like .htaccess files or other files not intended for the public.
- `body_buffer_size` (String) If the request exceeds this size, it will be written to disk. Enter a number and a unit like 1m.
- `ca` (Set of String) Trusted CA certificates.
- `certificate` (String) TLS Certificate.
- `charset` (String) Charset. One of `utf-8`.
- `client_header_buffer_size` (Number) Contains the size of a header Buffer. If a header or the request line does not fit into it, a large header buffer will be used.
- `default_server` (Boolean) Default Server.
- `disable_bot_protection` (Boolean) Blocks the request when a possibly bad bot is detected and adds the originating IP to the managed firewall alias for permanent blocking.
- `disable_gzip` (Boolean) Disables responses gzipping. Makes sense if TLS is used and this method of BREACH attack protection is preferred.
- `enable_acme_support` (Boolean) Enable Let's Encrypt Plugin Support.
- `enable_http3` (Boolean) Enable HTTP/3/QUIC for this server (adds QUIC listeners and Alt-Svc header).
- `error_log_level` (String) Select Error Log Level. Log levels are listed in the order of increasing verbosity. Setting a certain log level will cause all messages of the specified and more severe log levels to be logged. One of `emerg`, `alert`, `crit`, `error`, `warn`, `notice`, `info`.
- `errorpages` (Set of String) Select custom error pages to display instead of the default builtin error pages. If at least one error page is selected here, all default error pages will be disabled.
- `http2` (Boolean) Enable the HTTP/2 protocol.
- `https_only` (Boolean) If the request scheme is not HTTPS, redirect to use HTTPS for this server.
- `ip_acl` (String) If you select an IP ACL, the client can only access this service if it fulfills this requirement.
- `large_client_header_buffers_number` (Number) This field contains the amount of large header buffers. If there are not enough, the server will respond with an HTTP error.
- `large_client_header_buffers_size` (Number) This field contains the size of large header buffers. If a header or the request line does not fit into it, the server will respond with an HTTP error.
- `limit_request_connections` (Set of String) If you choose multiple limits, the strictest will be used.
- `listen_http_address` (Set of String) Enter a list of IP addresses and ports which can be used in nginx listen directives. To listen on a port on all IPs, use for example "80,[::]:80".
- `listen_https_address` (Set of String) Enter a list of IP addresses and ports which can be used in nginx listen directives. To listen on a port on all IPs, use for example "443,[::]:443".
- `locations` (Set of String) Locations.
- `log_handshakes` (Boolean) Log TLS handshakes to fill the User Agent fingerprint database and detect MITM attacks.
- `max_body_size` (String) If the request is larger, it will be rejectet with error 413 (Request Entity Too Large). For example, you can enter 200m.
- `naxsi_extensive_log` (Boolean) Provide a more verbose WAF log for fixing false positives before going live.
- `naxsi_whitelist_srcip` (Set of String) Enter a list of IP addresses or CIDR networks which will be whitelisted for the Naxsi rules.
- `ocsp_stapling` (Boolean) If you check this box, OCSP stapling is enabled. If your certificate has the TLS feature "status_request" enabled and don't enable OCSP Stapling, you could get an TLS error like "MOZILLA_PKIX_ERROR_REQUIRED_TLS_FEATURE_MISSING". This can be the case if you use Let's Encrypt with "OCSP Must Staple". More information about OCSP stapling can be found in RFC 7633.
- `ocsp_verify` (Boolean) Enables or disables verification of OCSP responses by the server.
- `proxy_intercept_errors` (Boolean) Intercept responses with codes greater than or equal to 300 and redirect to processing with custom error pages.
- `proxy_protocol` (Boolean) If you enable the proxy protocol, a downstream proxy can send the client IP and port before the real traffic is set.
- `real_ip_source` (String) X-Real-IP and X-Forwarded-For are HTTP headers, while PROXY protocol is a protocol which needs to be enabled. One of `X-Real-IP`, `X-Forwarded-For`, `proxy_protocol`, `CF-Connecting-IP`.
- `resolver` (String) Specify resolver for Upstream names resolution, OCSP stapling etc. Uses system resolver if not specified but can produce warning messages in log.
- `rewrites` (Set of String) Choose URL rewriting rules.
- `root` (String) File System Root.
- `satisfy` (String) All: All access restrictions must be fulfilled; Any: Any of the access restrictions must be fulfilled. One of `any`, `all`.
- `security_header` (String) Security Header.
- `sendfile` (Boolean) Allow the daemon to use the sendfile function.
- `servername` (Set of String) Server Name.
- `syslog_targets` (Set of String) SYSLOG targets.
- `tls_ciphers` (String) Specify enabled ciphers in the TLS library cipher string format. Example: ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256:ECDHE-RSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256. NGINX default (empty field): HIGH:!aNULL:!MD5.
- `tls_ecdh_curve` (String) Specify a curve(s) for ECDHE ciphers. NGINX default (empty field): auto.
- `tls_prefer_server_ciphers` (Boolean) Prefers server ciphers over client ciphers.
- `tls_protocols` (Set of String) Enable specified protocols. Default: TLSv1.2 TLSv1.3. TLSv1 and TLSv1.1 are insecure and excluded from GUI. One of `TLSv1.2`, `TLSv1.3`.
- `tls_reject_handshake` (Boolean) If enabled, TLS handshakes for this server will be rejected.
- `trusted_proxies` (Set of String) Enter a list of IP addresses or CIDR networks which are allowed to override the source IP address using the specified header.
- `trusted_proxies_alias` (String) Choose a Firewall Alias for trusted proxies.
- `verify_client` (String) On: the certificate is requested and validated. Use this option to protect a service with TLS authentication.Off: The certificate is not requested. Choose this option for a normal website.Optional: The certificate is requested and validated if existing. Choose this option for websites, with TLS login support or mixed TLS protected API and web content.Optional, don't verify: Do accept the certificate and let the application choose what to do. Choose this option, for the same reasons as optional but in this case, the request is passed to the backend without rejecting untrusted certificates. One of `off`, `on`, `optional`, `optional_no_ca`.
- `zero_rtt` (Boolean) If you enable this feature, your website will may get vulnerable to replay attacks, but you gain a big performance boost. You can read RFC 8446 for more information. The Backend will get a HTTP header "Early-Data" which can be used if a short handshake was used. If a response is too risky, answer with HTTP status code 425.
